claim: ESPHome implements availability with a retained birth message 'online' to <TOPIC_PREFIX>/status on connect plus a broker-side LWT 'offline' on connection drop, and HA marks all of the node's entities unavailable when the node is not connected.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should adopt the same retained birth + LWT pattern on a status topic for fleet-wide availability semantics
scope_conditions: ESPHome MQTT component; HA as subscriber
quoted_support: By default, ESPHome will send a retained MQTT message to <TOPIC_PREFIX>/status with payload online, and will tell the broker to send a message <TOPIC_PREFIX>/status with payload offline if the connection drops. If the node is not connected to MQTT, Home Assistant will show all its entities as unavailable

claim: Availability reporting is disabled when the birth message and last-will message have empty topics or topics that differ from each other.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must use ONE identical status topic for birth and LWT or availability breaks
quoted_support: If the birth message and last will message have empty topics or topics that are different from each other, availability reporting will be disabled.

claim: ESPHome offers shutdown_message for clean shutdowns, covering the case LWT cannot (LWT fires only on ungraceful disconnect).
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should publish a shutdown/offline message on SIGTERM-graceful stops, since systemd stops are graceful and LWT will not fire
quoted_support: shutdown_message (Optional, MQTTMessage): The message to send when the node shuts down and the connection is closed cleanly. See Last Will And Birth Messages for more information.

claim: ESPHome reboots a node after 15 minutes without an MQTT connection by default (reboot_timeout), a self-healing pattern for stuck connections.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent systemd unit should use WatchdogSec/Restart to bound time spent in a dead-connection state; ESPHome treats 15min as the ceiling
scope_conditions: ESPHome MQTT component, default 15min, configurable, 0s disables
quoted_support: reboot_timeout (Optional, Time): The amount of time to wait before rebooting when no MQTT connection exists. Can be disabled by setting this to 0s. Defaults to 15min.

claim: Stale retained discovery messages cause old entities to reappear on every HA restart; ESPHome ships a clean-mqtt helper that purges retained messages under <DISCOVERY_PREFIX>/+/NODE_NAME/#.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent needs a discovery-message hygiene story (retention + purge on uninstall) or removed entities will haunt HA across restarts
quoted_support: in order to have Home Assistant "discover" your devices on restart, all discovery MQTT messages need to be retained. Therefore the old entities will also re-appear on every Home Assistant restart even though they're in ESPHome anymore.

claim: HA 2021.12+ lets MQTT devices control generated entity names via object_id, and ESPHome's discovery_object_id_generator: device_name prefixes entity IDs with the device name (sensor.uptime -> sensor.<device name>_uptime) to disambiguate fleets of similar devices.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent fleet of N jupiterOS hosts must set object_id per entity (host-prefixed) or entity names will collide across hosts
quoted_support: Home Assistant 2021.12 allows MQTT devices to change this behaviour by specifying the object_id discovery attribute which replaces the sensor name part of the generated entity name.

claim: ESPHome's keepalive default is 15 seconds and shorter keepalive increases ping traffic; wait_for_connection blocks other components from starting until MQTT connects; publish_nan_as_none publishes None instead of NaN for HA Unknown/Unavailable states.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should expose keepalive tuning, optional connection-gated startup, and NaN->None conversion for HA state semantics
quoted_support: keepalive (Optional, Time): The time to keep the MQTT socket alive... Defaults to 15 seconds. ... wait_for_connection (Optional, bool): Blocks other components from starting until the MQTT connection is established. Defaults to false. ... publish_nan_as_none (Optional, bool): Publish None instead of NaN to handle Unknown/Unavailable sensor states in Home Assistant.

claim: ESPHome distinguishes device-level discovery (mqtt.discover_ip, esphome/discover topic with JSON ip/mac/version payload, used by the dashboard/CLI/HA) from entity-level HA MQTT discovery, and recommends disabling entity discovery when HA connects via the richer native API.
stance_target: jupiterOS fleet architecture: MQTT entity discovery vs native API is a deliberate two-tier choice; MQTT-only agents should stick with entity discovery
quoted_support: This can be achieved by enabling api and mqtt with mqtt.discover_ip enabled. It may makes sense to disable mqtt.discovery since there will be no need to use the MQTT entity discovery if Home Assistant will connect to the ESPHome API.
